system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: STABILITY NCT00799903 - The Stabilization of Atherosclerotic Plaque by Initiation of Darapladib Therapy Trial
Investigational drug: darapladib
Document: Darapladib effect on circulating high sensitive troponin in patients with acute coronary syndromes (journal, published 2012-08-05, source pmid:22963982)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Darapladib effect on circulating high sensitive troponin in patients with acute coronary syndromes

OBJECTIVES: We compared the incidence of late increase in hs-cTnI between ACS and non-ACS patients treated with standard of care with or without darapladib. METHODS: A total of 323 (161 ACS and 162 non-ACS patients) were included. High sensitivity troponin I was measured at baseline and at 4, 13, 26 and 52 weeks. RESULTS: ACS patients had statistically higher hs-cTnI values during longer term follow-up at which these patients were no longer in the acute setting of myocardial ischemia, but were regarded to have stable CAD (mean hsTnI value in ACS patients: 1.180 versus 0.886 ng/L in non-ACS patients, p = 0.02). Multivariate logistic regression revealed three predictors of any 2-fold increase in hs-cTnI levels compared to the previous visit when interactions were not considered. Treatment with darapladib (adjusted OR 0.53; 95% CI: 0.30-0.92) and initial presentation with ACS (adjusted OR 0.42; 95% CI: 0.23-0.77) were associated with less frequent occurrence of a 2-fold increase in hs-cTnI levels. In contrast, diabetes was associated with a higher incidence of 2-fold increases in hs-cTnI levels (adjusted OR 2.20; 95% CI: 1.04-4.64). Logistic regression to predict any 2-fold increase in hs-cTnI by ACS status showed that in the ACS group, treatment with darapladib decreased the risk of elevation of hs-cTnI (OR 0.219; 95% CI: 0.087, 0.553, p = 0.0013). CONCLUSION: In patients with ACS, treatment with darapladib is associated with less increase in cardiac troponin I compared to standard of care alone. This beneficial effect may be associated with darapladib's capability of reducing necrotic core in coronary plaques.
--- END ---
